subject: python
title: Variables and Assignment
description: Understanding variable naming, binding names to values, and the assignment operator '='.
learning_objectives: Define and assign variables in Python using '='
Understand that variables point to values in memory
Differentiate between variable declaration/assignment and algebraic equality

misconceptions.name: Confusing Assignment with Algebraic Equality
misconceptions.description: The student interprets 'x = x + 1' as impossible algebra rather than evaluating the right-hand side and binding to 'x'.
misconceptions.counter_example:
x = 5
x = x + 1
# In math this is impossible, but in Python x now points to 6.
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Explain '=' as an arrow '<-' pointing the computed result on the right into the box/label on the left.

misconceptions.name: Permanent Variable Linking
misconceptions.description: The student believes that after 'b = a', changing 'a' later will automatically update 'b'.
misconceptions.counter_example:
a = 10
b = a
a = 20
print(b) # prints 10, not 20
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Emphasize that assignment copies the value reference at that instant; it is not a reactive link.

misconceptions.name: Losing a Value During a Swap
misconceptions.description: The student writes x = y before saving x, so x's original value is overwritten and the swap loses data.
misconceptions.counter_example:
x = 1
y = 2
x = y  # x is now 2 too
y = x  # both are 2; x's original 1 is gone
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Before overwriting x, copy it into a third variable: temp = x.

misconceptions.name: Using an Undefined Temporary Variable
misconceptions.description: The student copies from a name that was never assigned, or uses a helper variable that has no value yet.
misconceptions.counter_example:
x = 1
y = 2
x = a  # NameError: name 'a' is not defined
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Create the helper from a real variable first, e.g. temp = x, then use it.

misconceptions.name: Reversing the Direction of Assignment
misconceptions.description: The student writes x = temp instead of temp = x, so the old or empty helper value flows into x instead of saving x.
misconceptions.counter_example:
temp = x  # correct: save x into temp
# x = temp would copy temp back into x instead of saving x
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Read '=' as an arrow pointing into the left name: the right side is computed and stored on the left.

subject: python
title: Primitive Data Types (int, float, str, bool)
description: Identifying and working with Python core types: integers, floating point numbers, strings, and booleans.
learning_objectives: Distinguish between int, float, str, and bool
Perform type checking and explicit conversion with int(), str(), float()

misconceptions.name: Conflating Numeric Strings with Integers
misconceptions.description: The student expects '"5" + "5"' to evaluate to 10 instead of string concatenation '"55"'.
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Point out quotes indicate text/letters. Show that text glued together gives '55', while numbers give 10.

misconceptions.name: Choosing the Wrong Conversion Function
misconceptions.description: The student uses str() or float() when whole-number arithmetic needs int(), or assumes Python converts text automatically.
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Use int() for whole-number text and float() for decimal text; str() only when you need text.

subject: python
title: Operators and Expressions
learning_objectives: Evaluate arithmetic expressions with correct precedence
Evaluate boolean comparison expressions returning True or False
Distinguish between single '=' (assign) and double '==' (equality test)

misconceptions.name: Floor Division vs Float Division
misconceptions.description: The student expects 7 / 2 to return integer 3, or confuses // with % modulo.
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Clarify that '/' always yields a decimal float in Python 3, whereas '//' chops off the decimal.

subject: python
title: Conditional Branching (if, elif, else)
description: Directing program flow based on boolean expressions and indentation blocks.
learning_objectives: Write multi-branch decisions using if, elif, and else
Understand block scope delineated by 4-space indentation
Predict which branch executes when multiple conditions evaluate

misconceptions.name: Multiple Ifs vs Elif Execution
misconceptions.description: The student writes multiple independent 'if' statements expecting mutual exclusivity.
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Illustrate that 'elif' forms a single connected chain where at most one branch can win.

subject: python
title: Lists and Sequences
description: Creating lists, indexing, slicing, and mutating ordered collections.
learning_objectives: Create lists containing primitive items
Access elements using 0-based indexing and negative indexing
Append and modify list elements

misconceptions.name: One-Based Indexing Assumption
misconceptions.description: The student accesses the first element with my_list[1] instead of my_list[0].
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Remind that computer indices measure offset from start; the very first item is at offset 0.

subject: python
title: For Loops and Iteration
description: Iterating over collections and number sequences using 'for' and 'range()'.
learning_objectives: Iterate over items in a list using 'for item in collection'
Generate sequences with range(start, stop, step)
Accumulate results across loop iterations

misconceptions.name: Expecting range(n) to Include n
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Explain the stop parameter in Python is always exclusive: 'up to but not including'.

subject: python
title: While Loops and Loop Control
description: Repetition governed by dynamic boolean conditions and terminating states.
learning_objectives: Construct while loops with initialization, condition, and update steps
Avoid infinite loops through deterministic state updates

misconceptions.name: Omission of Termination Variable Update
misconceptions.description: The student creates an infinite loop because the condition variable is never modified inside the loop body.
misconceptions.counter_example:
count = 0
while count < 3:
    print(count)
    # forgot count += 1 -> infinite loop!
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Teach the three-step checklist for while loops: initialize, check, update.

subject: python
title: Functions, Parameters, and Return Values
description: Encapsulating reusable logic using 'def', positional arguments, and explicit 'return' statements.
learning_objectives: Define functions with def, parameters, and docstrings
Distinguish returning a value from printing to console
Understand variable scope inside vs outside functions

misconceptions.name: Conflating Print with Return
misconceptions.description: The student uses print() inside a function and assumes callers receive the printed value, resulting in None.
misconceptions.counter_example:
def add(a, b):
    print(a + b)

res = add(2, 3)
print(res) # prints None! res is not 5.
misconceptions.remediation_hint: Explain that print() sends text to the screen for human eyes; return sends the value back to the code.
